findings.description: The loop condition uses len(self._keys_by_country), which is the number of distinct countries, not the number of cached entries. The cache is therefore effectively unbounded: with a few countries and many postal codes it never evicts, so memory grows without limit and max_entries is not honored. The comparison should use len(self._entries). The current check also fails to give the intended LRU bound when max_entries=1 with many postal codes.
findings.title: Eviction bound counts countries, not entries

findings.description: invalidate_country and clear remove entries without incrementing counters, which is fine, but the main defect is in the eviction path: _evict_oldest assumes _keys_by_country and _entries stay in sync. After the bound is fixed to count entries, this stays consistent. As written, clear() keeps hit/miss counters, so hit_ratio after clear mixes pre- and post-clear lookups. Minor, but it can mislead admins.
findings.suggestion: Document or reset counters in clear(), or leave as is deliberately.
findings.title: clear() does not reset stats, and the invalidation/eviction bookkeeping is inconsistent

findings.description: The loader runs while holding a non-reentrant threading.Lock. A slow loader blocks all lookups, including hits for other keys. If the loader ever calls back into the cache, it deadlocks. Misses for unknown jurisdictions raise after _misses was incremented, which is acceptable, but the global serialization of loads is a real throughput hazard.
findings.suggestion: Load outside the lock and use a per-country generation counter to avoid storing superseded rates.
findings.title: Loader exception path counts a miss and holds a non-reentrant lock during I/O

findings.description: source.replace_country runs first, and rates_changed runs afterward. Between the two calls, concurrent lookups can still hit cached old rates. A concurrent miss in that window can also load the new rate and then be dropped. The rate seen by invoices may be stale for a short time. TableRateSource is also mutated without any lock while rate_for reads it from the cache thread.
findings.suggestion: Do the replace and invalidate under a shared lock, or accept and document the window.
findings.title: Table replaced before cache invalidation leaves a stale window
